title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a formal response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its commitment to address the key concerns raised about AI safety, transparency, and accountability. It proposes a set of policy measures and regulatory frameworks aimed at ensuring AI systems meet public standards and protect citizens' interests.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual will set clear rules to oversee how artificial intelligence can be used in exams and qualifications, ensuring fairness and maintaining assessment integrity. The policy aims to protect learners, keep public confidence high, and encourage responsible AI use in the education sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report evaluates how copyright-protected works are used to train AI systems and the legal, economic, and societal impacts of such use. It offers recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with AI development and suggests policy measures to address potential conflicts.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a formal reply to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” In its response, the government outlines its commitments and actions to address the report’s recommendations for strengthening AI regulation, investment, and ethical standards across the country.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the duties, scope, and goals of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence should meet public standards. It also provides frequently asked questions that explain the committee’s procedures, responsibilities, and the criteria it will use to evaluate AI against societal expectations.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. Their submission is intended to inform the committee on best practices, challenges, and policy recommendations for managing AI’s societal impact.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy outlines how artificial intelligence will reshape the rules and oversight for medical products, aiming to ensure safety, effectiveness, and transparency. It emphasizes applying the AI White Paper principles to guide regulatory updates and foster responsible innovation in healthcare.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to position the organisation as the leading AI‑driven defence entity for its size, focusing on effectiveness, efficiency, trust, and influence. It outlines a plan to develop and deploy advanced AI capabilities that enhance operational performance while upholding ethical and strategic standards.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness the benefits of AI while mitigating its risks. It outlines strategies for collaboration, investment, and safety measures to ensure AI technologies are used responsibly across the industry.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report looks at how AI developers use copyrighted works and checks if they’re following Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It shares progress made, notes key challenges, and offers recommendations for balancing AI innovation with copyright protection.
